Tiers: A=peer-reviewed (PubMed/NEJM/BMJ/Cochrane), B=expert content (Attia/Huberman/Baar/Beck/university .edu), C=mainstream medical/IOF, D=Thai official.

sources.org: Journal of Bone and Mineral Research / PubMed
sources.reliability_notes: Watson, Weeks, Beck et al. 2018 — LIFTMOR RCT: HiRIT increased lumbar BMD +2.9% vs -1.2% in postmenopausal women with osteopenia/osteoporosis (landmark)
Harding, Beck et al. 2020 — LIFTMOR-M: replicated HiRIT BMD gains in older men with low BMD
Knapen, Vermeer et al. 2013 — 3-year 180 µg/day MK-7 RCT: slowed BMD loss at lumbar spine and femoral neck in 244 postmenopausal women
Geleijnse, Vermeer et al. 2004 — Rotterdam Study: dietary K2 (menaquinone) highest tertile linked to 57% lower CHD risk, 52% less aortic calcification
Clegg et al. 2006 — GAIT trial (N=1,583): glucosamine+chondroitin not superior to placebo overall, but positive signal in moderate-severe pain subgroup
Lugo/Crolla et al. 2016 — UC-II 40 mg/day vs glucosamine 1,500 + chondroitin 1,200 in 191 knee OA patients: UC-II reduced WOMAC 39% vs 18%

sources.org: International Journal of Medical Sciences / PubMed
sources.reliability_notes: Crowley et al. 2009 — pilot safety/efficacy trial of undenatured type II collagen (UC-II) for knee osteoarthritis

sources.org: New England Journal of Medicine / PubMed
sources.reliability_notes: Bischoff-Ferrari et al. 2012 — pooled analysis of 11 RCTs (N=31,022): vitamin D ≥800 IU/day reduced hip fracture risk ~30% in people ≥65 y
DIPART Group 2010 — 68,517-patient pooled meta-analysis: Ca+D reduced total fractures ~8%, hip ~16%
Haentjens et al. 2010 — 22-study meta-analysis: excess 1-year mortality after hip fracture 5-8× in men, 2-3× in women, persists ~10 y
Marshall, Johnell, Wedel 1996 — seminal meta-analysis: each 1-SD drop in BMD ~doubles fracture risk (WHO threshold basis)
WHO 1994 — defined osteoporosis T-score ≤ -2.5 SD on DEXA

sources.org: Endocrinology & Metabolism Clinics of North America / PubMed
sources.reliability_notes: Khosla & Riggs 2011 — postmenopausal osteoporosis review (BMD loss rates)
Physiology, Bone Remodeling — open peer-reviewed reference; BMU cycle, ~10%/y turnover
Uwitonze & Razzaque 2018 — Role of Magnesium in Vitamin D Activation and Function (25-hydroxylase, 1α-hydroxylase cofactor)
König, Oesser et al. 2018 — 131 postmenopausal women, 5 g/day specific collagen peptides 12 mo, +BMD spine/femoral neck

sources.org: American Journal of Clinical Nutrition / PubMed
sources.reliability_notes: Shaw, Baar et al. 2017 — gelatin + vitamin C before impact doubled collagen synthesis (PINP) — Baar protocol anchor

sources.org: Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews / PubMed
sources.reliability_notes: Bellamy et al. 2015 — Cochrane review: intra-articular HA 2-6 months pain relief in knee OA
Debbi et al. 2011 — 3 g/day MSM vs placebo 12 weeks: significant WOMAC pain/function improvement
Bruyère et al. 2008 — crystalline glucosamine sulfate 1,500 mg/day ≥12 mo reduced 5-y risk of total knee replacement ~50%
Histology, Collagen — 28 collagen types; Type I ~90% of body, Type II ~90-95% of cartilage
Feskanich, Willett 1997 — Nurses' Health Study (77,761 women, 12 y): high milk intake did NOT reduce hip fracture risk
Michaëlsson et al. 2014 — Swedish cohort (~106,000): high milk intake linked to higher fracture and mortality in women
Bolland et al. 2015 — systematic review: calcium alone (diet or supplement) did NOT significantly reduce fractures in RCTs
Heaney, Dowell, Barger-Lux 1999 — calcium bioavailability: citrate vs carbonate absorption and pH dependence
Kawchuk et al. 2015 — real-time MRI of knuckle cavitation: joint 'cracking' is gas bubble formation in synovial fluid
2018 USPSTF recommendation — DEXA screening for osteoporosis in women ≥65
Chailurkit et al. — Thai vitamin D insufficiency ≥50% of adults (Thai national data)
Weaver et al. 2016 — NOF position statement on peak bone mass (ages 20-30 window)
Sophia Fox, Bedi, Rodeo 2009 — articular cartilage structure and injury review (friction coefficient, water content)
Khosla et al. 2008 — estrogen, RANKL/OPG, and bone resorption mechanism
Cummings et al. 2009 — FREEDOM trial: denosumab (anti-RANKL) reduced vertebral fractures 68% in postmenopausal osteoporosis
Delgado-Calle, Bellido 2013 — sclerostin regulation of bone formation and Wnt/β-catenin pathway
NIH ODS Vitamin D fact sheet — dosing, RDA, safety
Gröber, Schmidt, Kisters 2013 — Magnesium in Prevention and Therapy review (~48% US below RDA)
Troeberg, Nagase 2012 — MMPs and aggrecanases in cartilage degradation
Band et al. 2016 — hyaluronan, pain, inflammation, and role of synovial fluid in OA
Goldring, Otero — Osteoarthritis pathomechanisms year-in-review (IL-1β, MMP-13, ADAMTS-5)
OARSI 2019 — White Paper on OA as a Serious Disease (guideline body)
IOF — 1/3 women, 1/5 men ≥50 fragility fracture risk; fracture every 3 seconds globally
NIH NIAMS official osteoporosis overview (US federal authority)
